summary: Summation No. 30 covers March 1948, the month in which Hitoshi Ashida formed a coalition cabinet of Democrats (six), Social Democrats (eight) and People's Cooperative Party members (two) on the basis of a three-party policy agreement. It reports the new Police Reorganization Law taking effect on 7 March, the founding of the Democratic Liberal Party on 15 March, the reconvened Second Diet and the Prime Minister's policy address, the winding up of the purge screening committees by 10 May, discoveries of hoarded goods, and the defense summation at the International Military Tribunal. The economic sections give February and March statistics on agriculture, mining, heavy industry, textiles, communications, labor disputes (coal, electric power, express transport), trade, rationing, prices, banking and finance, science and technology. Social sections cover communicable disease, public assistance, repatriation, vital statistics, education, religion and the media. Historians will find the detailed cabinet formation narrative, party realignments and production and finance tables especially useful.
highlights: A three-party policy agreement among the Democratic, Social Democratic and People's Cooperative Parties, with concessions to the Social Democratic left wing, let Prime Minister Hitoshi Ashida form a cabinet of six Democrats, eight Social Democrats and two People's Cooperative members.
The Liberal Party and minor groups formed the Democratic Liberal Party on 15 March, the largest Diet group, with 153 members in the House of Representatives and 44 in the House of Councillors.
The Police Reorganization Law took effect 7 March, and autonomous police forces were set up in all 1,605 municipalities with populations over 5,000; the shokutaku system was abolished on 31 March.

Purge screening examined 674,579 persons, removing 4,861 from office and barring 2,816; 165 of 1,424 information-media executives were barred, and public-office screening committees were to end on 10 May.

The Second National Diet reconvened on 20 March; Ashida gave his administrative address and Economic Stabilization Board head Kuroki outlined economic policy, followed by interpellations on 22-25 March.
At the International Military Tribunal the defense summation ran from 2 to 31 March, arguing that ex-post-facto penalization of Japanese leaders might be seen as a gross injustice.

Labor disputes included coal-miner wage demands, a mediated settlement accepted 25 March by the electric power union, an express company union award on 9 March, and the arrest of 13 union officials at Aikodo Printing.

Bank of Japan notes outstanding reached 218,775,000,000 yen on 31 March, Reconstruction Finance Bank loans totaled 54,439,200,000 yen on 29 February, and February land sales to tenants were 61,857 cho.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover for Summation No. 30 (March 1948), table of contents by part and section, lists of charts, maps and graphs (94 items), and the map of Japan.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: no change in SCAP organization, formation of the Ashida cabinet, police reform, purge figures, war crimes trials, and economic and social highlights.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: No change occurred in the non-military organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during March.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Covers the Ashida coalition cabinet, the 7 March police law, the Democratic Liberal Party's 153 House seats, the Diet reconvening on 20 March, purge totals, crime figures and war crimes trials.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: February output rose in coke, copper, textiles and power; cement fell to 85,358 tons. SCAP warned on 29 March that communications work stoppages breached its 31 January 1947 strike statement; the Diet passed Supplementary Budget No. 15.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Tokyo opened a Model Health Center demonstrating 12 basic health services; the Japan Medical Association was reorganized; 12 institutions became four-year universities; press debated the Ashida cabinet and the new ¥2,920 wage base.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Detailed account of the Ashida cabinet formation, parties, Diet and purge, police and prison statistics, Japanese courts, and war crimes trials including the Tokyo tribunal's defense summation.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Narrates the Ashida cabinet formation, hoarded goods, budgets, the police reorganization, party realignment, the Diet session and the winding up of the purge committees.

sections.title: Political Developments: Formation of New Cabinet
sections.summary: Three-party policy agreement, left-wing Social Democratic reaction, cabinet membership, the Prime Minister's statement, and ministers' policy statements with biographical sketches.

sections.title: Hoarded Goods
sections.summary: Procurators found goods worth $9,000,000,000 at former Nakajima Aircraft plants, and Gifu Diet member Keichi Yamamoto was indicted. A 27 March ordinance, effective 31 March, required declaration of undeclared stocks, with false reports confiscated.

sections.title: National Government
sections.summary: Cabinet agreed on 1948-49 budgets and three supplementary budgets passed; the new police system began 7 March and the shokutaku system was abolished.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: Positions of the Democratic, Social Democratic, People's Cooperative, Liberal, Social Renovation and Communist parties and the Green Breeze Society; the Democratic Liberal Party formed 15 March.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: Ashida's administrative address, party comments, interpellations by Saito, Asanuma and Itaya, Director General Kuroki's economic address, and bills enacted and introduced.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: Public office and information media screening results, loss of records, and discontinuance of the purge committees by 10 May.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: Black-market and crime reports and police reorganization; 146,669 offenses and 76,802 arrests in January, and 83,872 prisoners on 29 February.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: Supreme Court caseload, 78 atrocity investigations, 12 trials of 73 suspects, and Tokyo tribunal summations on Shiratori, Suzuki, Togo, Tojo and Umezu, and defense of Hata, Doihara and Hiranuma.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Statistical sector reports for February-March 1948 on agriculture, mining, industry, textiles, transport, communications, labor, trade, rationing, finance, property control and science.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Land sales to tenants reached 61,857 cho in February (cumulative 280,763 cho); also livestock slaughter, sericulture, marine landings, fishing petroleum allocations and whaling.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: February log production of 71,133,700 cubic feet, plus firewood and charcoal output, coal production and deliveries, crude oil drilling and mine production.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: February coke output of 192,570 metric tons; also iron and steel, nonferrous rolling, cement, shipbuilding, chemicals, machine tools, industrial machinery and rolling stock.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: February pulp output rose to 29,313 tons from 23,230; window glass fell 18,903 cases; Nissan led truck chassis (511 units); bicycles reached 38,011; three-wheelers hit a postwar high of 952; watches and sewing machines also set highs.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: Cotton fabric output at a postwar high, raw silk back to December level, rayon increases, and wool, bast fiber, knit goods and clothing supply and stock tables.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: 156,740 registered commercial vehicles in February; rail traffic indexes, water-borne cargo, air transport, and electric energy and gas generation and consumption.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: Competitive bidding reached 35 percent of telecommunications contract value; 1,179,972 telephones in service on 29 February; 6,330,057 radio licensees; Hongkong radiotelegraph circuit opened 1 March; 436,732 employees; Supplementary Budget No. 10 raised wages to the ¥2,920 level.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Kanju Kato named Labor Minister; union membership, coal, electric power and express-company wage disputes, the Aikodo Printing production-control case, wages and employment.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: January private trade approvals of 21 import contracts ($1,838,395) and 839 export contracts ($6,050,598), with breakdowns by country, balances and commodities.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Staple crop collection quota exceeded by 0.9 percent, rice stocks near 3,000,000 tons, consumer price index and ten rationed commodities.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes stood at 218,775,000,000 yen on 31 March; Reconstruction Finance Bank loans were 54,439,200,000 yen; also banks, deposit bureau, securities liquidation and budget.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: Looted property worth 436,000 yen reported and 35,000 yen restituted; also looted ships, antitrust and cartel actions, and reparations.

sections.title: Section 13. Science and Technology
sections.summary: Renewal Committee for the Organization of Science met 23-24 February; also research activities, personnel, patents and standards, and publications.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Model health center opened 15 March; also public health, welfare, education, religion and media reports, repatriation, vital statistics and SCAP information libraries.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Model Health Center opened in Tokyo 15 March; communicable diseases, medical supplies, narcotics, public assistance, LARA relief, repatriation and vital statistics.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion, Cultural Resources and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Teacher salary study, teacher conferences, Catholic church statistics, national treasures, press, radio, films, theater, music, and SCAP libraries with 48,729 visits; ends with map page.
